days.title: The MOSFET as a Controlled Switch

questions.prompt: In the useful first-order model of an enhancement-mode nMOS, what primarily controls whether a conductive channel forms?
options: The gate-to-source voltage relative to threshold
A steady current through the insulated gate
The drain voltage alone, independent of the source
The Boolean name assigned to the drain node
questions.explanation: An electric field produced by gate-to-source voltage changes channel conductivity. The insulated gate ideally draws negligible steady current; real behavior also depends on terminal voltages, geometry, process, and temperature.

questions.prompt: Why is a MOSFET called a controlled switch only as an abstraction?
options: It can represent only decimal values
Its output changes without moving charge
It is either a perfect short or perfect open at every voltage
It has finite resistance, capacitance, leakage, and a gradual voltage-dependent transition
questions.explanation: The switch model is useful for logic reasoning, but a real device has analog current-voltage behavior, parasitic capacitance, finite on-resistance, subthreshold leakage, and process/temperature variation.

questions.prompt: What physically changes when a MOSFET-driven output node rises in voltage?
options: The insulated gate supplies a continuous DC output current
Every transistor connected to the node becomes an ideal wire
Charge accumulates on the node's effective capacitance
The node's Boolean label changes without energy transfer
questions.explanation: A node includes device, wire, and receiver capacitances. Raising its voltage requires moving charge onto that capacitance; lowering it removes charge.

questions.prompt: Why is a lone nMOS pass device poor at passing a strong logic-high level in the simple threshold model?
options: A logic high requires no current path
As the output rises, gate-to-source voltage falls until channel conduction weakens near a threshold below the gate voltage
nMOS devices can conduct only when their drain is exactly zero
The source node cannot hold charge
questions.explanation: With a fixed high gate, a rising source reduces VGS. Conduction weakens as VGS approaches threshold, so the passed high is degraded; complementary CMOS avoids relying on that weak-high path for restoration.

questions.prompt: For a settled CMOS inverter with a low input, which intended conduction state produces a high output?
options: pMOS on and nMOS off
pMOS off and nMOS on
Both devices held fully on
Both devices held fully off with no previous charge
questions.explanation: A low input turns the pMOS pull-up on and the nMOS pull-down off, providing a path to VDD and no intended DC path to ground.

questions.prompt: What does logic-level restoration mean?
options: Every input voltage is copied exactly to the output
The inverter stores its output forever without power
Noise is mathematically impossible on a CMOS wire
An input within a valid logic range drives the output toward a supply rail rather than reproducing every analog deviation
questions.explanation: A restoring gate maps valid but imperfect input ranges to outputs near the rails, allowing digital stages to compose despite bounded analog disturbance.

questions.prompt: What does a positive noise margin quantify?
options: The time between two clock edges
The maximum DC current through an ideal gate oxide
The allowable separation between a guaranteed output level and the next gate's required input threshold
The number of transistors in the inverter
questions.explanation: High and low noise margins compare guaranteed output levels with accepted input thresholds. They measure how much disturbance can be tolerated while preserving logical interpretation.

questions.prompt: Why can a CMOS inverter draw transient supply current while switching even if settled static current is small?
options: The gate oxide becomes an intentional DC resistor
It must charge or discharge capacitance, and both networks may partially conduct during the transition
The output changes without any charge movement
Only leakage exists during transitions
questions.explanation: Dynamic charging current and brief short-circuit current occur during transitions. Idealized low settled static current does not imply zero switching energy.

questions.prompt: In a two-input CMOS NAND pull-down network, how are the nMOS devices arranged?
options: In series, so both inputs must be high to pull the output low
In parallel, so either high input pulls the output low
As two permanently conducting resistors
Disconnected from the output
questions.explanation: The NAND output is low only for A=1 and B=1, so its nMOS pull-down path requires both series devices to conduct. The complementary pMOS pull-up devices are parallel.

questions.prompt: Why must the pull-up network implement the complement of the pull-down conduction condition?
options: Both networks must provide a permanent VDD-to-ground path
It guarantees zero propagation delay
It changes a NAND into an analog amplifier only
For each valid settled input, exactly one network should provide the restoring path to a rail
questions.explanation: Complementary conduction avoids an undefined floating output and avoids an intended static short between rails for valid settled inputs.

questions.prompt: What Boolean transformation is especially useful when deriving complementary series/parallel CMOS networks?
options: Two's-complement negation only
ASCII encoding
De Morgan's laws
The quadratic formula
questions.explanation: De Morgan's laws relate complemented AND/OR functions and mirror the way series and parallel conditions exchange between pull-down and pull-up networks.

questions.prompt: Why is a complex CMOS gate not accurately described by its truth table alone?
options: All logically equivalent networks have identical analog behavior
Topology, transistor sizing, internal capacitance, input order, and loading affect delay and power
Truth tables already specify exact wire geometry
Boolean behavior determines a unique transistor layout
questions.explanation: The truth table specifies settled logic behavior, while physical topology and loading determine transition behavior, energy, and robustness.

questions.prompt: Why does increasing a gate's capacitive load usually increase propagation delay?
options: Finite drive current must move more charge to change the node voltage
Capacitance removes the need for current
The Boolean function gains another truth-table row
A larger load always lowers the supply voltage to zero
questions.explanation: A larger effective capacitance requires more charge for the same voltage swing. With finite drive strength, that generally lengthens rise or fall time and threshold-crossing delay.

questions.prompt: What does fan-out mean in the electrical timing discussion?
options: The number of source-code files in a module
The number of clock cycles in a program
The number of voltage rails
The load presented by driven inputs and interconnect, not merely an abstract count
questions.explanation: Receiver gates and wires contribute capacitance. A count can be a shorthand only when those loads are comparable; electrical load is what affects the driver.

questions.prompt: In the approximation Pdynamic ≈ alpha C V² f, what does alpha represent?
options: Static leakage resistance
Clock-to-Q delay
Switching activity: the fraction/rate of relevant charging transitions
A universal transistor count
questions.explanation: Alpha captures activity. The relation is a useful proportional model, not a complete chip power equation; glitching, short-circuit current, leakage, and clock distribution also matter.

questions.prompt: Why can logically correct combinational logic still fail in a synchronous CPU?
options: A correct Boolean function always has zero delay
Its worst-case result may arrive too late for the capture register's setup requirement
Truth tables prohibit clocks
Registers accept data only when no gates are present
questions.explanation: Boolean correctness says what value eventually results. Timing correctness asks whether it arrives within the required clock window across relevant paths and conditions.

questions.prompt: What does a setup-time requirement constrain?
options: How long input data must be stable before the active capture edge
How long the clock must remain permanently high
The number of transistors in the data source
Only the output voltage after reset
questions.explanation: Setup time defines a pre-edge stability window needed for reliable capture under the characterized conditions.

questions.prompt: What does a hold-time requirement constrain?
options: The maximum period between clock edges
How long reset must remain asserted before power-on
Only combinational outputs with no register
How long input data must remain stable after the active capture edge
questions.explanation: Hold time is the post-edge stability requirement. Fast contamination paths and clock skew can violate hold even when the clock period is made longer.

questions.prompt: What is metastability in a bistable storage element?
options: A deterministic one-cycle delay inserted by every flip-flop
A synthesis syntax error
An analog condition that can take an unbounded-in-principle time to resolve after a timing violation
A third architectural bit value software can reliably read
questions.explanation: A violated sampling window can leave internal nodes near an unstable balance. Resolution probability improves with time, but no finite synchronizer makes the risk mathematically zero.

questions.prompt: Why is a two-flop synchronizer appropriate for a single asynchronous control bit but not a complete solution for an arbitrary multi-bit bus?
options: Metastability occurs only in combinational gates
Bits can resolve or be sampled in different cycles, so the bus may be incoherent
Two flip-flops cannot store Boolean values
Multi-bit buses never cross clock domains
questions.explanation: Independent bit synchronization does not preserve a coherent multi-bit word. Handshakes, Gray codes, asynchronous FIFOs, or other CDC protocols are used according to the transfer.

questions.prompt: Why should an always_comb block assign its output on every control path?
options: Otherwise retaining the previous value implies unintended storage rather than pure combinational logic
Because combinational logic may contain only one operator
Because a simulator cannot evaluate if statements
To force every output permanently to zero
questions.explanation: Complete assignment defines an output for every input combination. Missing paths request value retention, which requires state and commonly indicates accidental latch inference.

questions.prompt: Why are nonblocking assignments conventionally used for clocked sequential RTL?
options: They make all arithmetic execute instantly in silicon
They are the only assignments a simulator accepts
They automatically create an asynchronous clock
Their update scheduling models simultaneous register sampling and avoids order-dependent procedural races
questions.explanation: Clocked processes conceptually sample old state at the edge and publish updates afterward. Nonblocking assignment scheduling represents that behavior and reduces source-order artifacts.

questions.prompt: In the ALU register-stage lab, what is the architectural distinction between alu_result and result_out?
options: result_out is a testbench-only print operation
alu_result stores data through power loss
alu_result is combinational next data; result_out is state captured on a clock edge
Both are independent clocks
questions.explanation: The ALU result responds combinationally to current inputs and operation selection. The output register changes at an active edge according to reset/valid behavior.

questions.prompt: What can an RTL simulation demonstrate directly?
options: That every possible input sequence is correct from one test
Behavior of the simulated model for the applied stimulus and assertions
Final post-route timing across all silicon corners
A transistor-accurate power number without device models
questions.explanation: Simulation is evidence about a particular model and exercised scenarios. Coverage, properties, synthesis, timing, and physical analyses answer additional questions.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best describes the conceptual RTL synthesis path?
options: Elaboration, generic inference, optimization, then technology mapping
Routing, C compilation, transistor fabrication, then simulation
Placement, page-table walk, linking, then elaboration
Simulation alone followed directly by silicon
questions.explanation: Elaboration resolves the concrete design, inference creates generic operations/state, optimization transforms equivalent structure, and mapping selects target-supported resources.

questions.prompt: Why might a source-level addition not remain as one adder cell in the final netlist?
options: Synthesis tools cannot implement arithmetic
Every plus operator is treated as a simulator delay
Placement always deletes arithmetic
Constant propagation, width reduction, target mapping, or other equivalent rewrites can reshape or remove it
questions.explanation: Synthesis preserves required behavior rather than source spelling. An addition by zero can disappear, constants can simplify it, and a target can implement arithmetic with different primitive structures.

questions.prompt: What has not been created merely because Yosys emitted a mapped generic netlist?
options: Any inferred combinational logic
Any named top module
Physical placement, routed wires, extracted parasitics, and signoff timing
Any representation of connectivity
questions.explanation: A logical netlist captures cells/operations and connections. Physical implementation and signoff require target-specific floorplanning, placement, clocking, routing, extraction, and checks.

questions.prompt: How does this synthesis lesson reconnect to systems programming?
options: It requires every systems programmer to specialize in ASIC layout
It explains the implementation beneath ISA-visible state before returning to microarchitecture, MMU/privilege, exceptions, and ToyOS
It replaces the need to understand the ISA or operating systems
It proves software source maps one-to-one onto transistors
questions.explanation: The chip material supplies causal depth beneath the ISA. The course then moves upward through CPU mechanisms used by kernels: pipelines, memory translation, privilege, exceptions, and OS construction.
